Ready for the maintainer to merge.

The review found no blocking items.

- The G82 and G89 signatures include the dwell. A changed dwell closes the cycle with G80 and starts it again.
- G89 writes P0 for zero dwell. Equal dwells keep the open cycle group.
- The change keeps the G83 behaviour. The tests and decision record cover issue #2350.
- No golden files changed. No UI, dependency, build script, workflow or process files changed.

The review used the current `upstream/main:AGENTS.md`.
The local worktree was `.claude/worktrees/review-2355`, with its own target directory.
The trial merge used upstream main `94f7d6b891668e38882b2e7d4f3730b9a2787f24`.
Git reported "Already up to date." The PR contains that main commit.
No GitHub runner was used.

Safety mutation checks:

I ran the local post CLI with six input cases for each script variant.
The cases match the new test inputs: changed G82 dwell, changed G89 dwell, two zero-dwell G89 cases, and equal dwells.
The script copies and output files were in `/tmp`. The tracked files stayed unchanged.

1. Original upstream post: four cases failed as expected. Changed dwells kept the previous P, and a zero-dwell G89 omitted P.
2. Fixed signatures with the old P condition: both zero-dwell G89 cases failed as expected. The cycle reopened but omitted P0.
3. Fixed post: all six cases passed. Each changed dwell had G80 between the two cycle blocks.

Reference: the public [Haas G89 page](https://www.haascnc.com/service/codes-settings.type%3Dgcode.machine%3Dmill.value%3DG89.html) states that P values are modal.
No physical Haas control was tested.

Requested before merge: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 17be0f00b685b318cf18953f8679878acf70b098 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Independent review (safety floor: this change alters posted G-code). No blockers.

### What looks good
- `assets/posts/haas.cps` `onCycle`: the dwell (`ms`) is now in the open-cycle signature for G82, G83 and G89. A changed dwell writes `G80` and issues the cycle again with its own P. Holes with the same dwell stay in the open group as bare `X Y` blocks.
- G82 is selected only for `ms > 0`, so each G82 block carries a positive P. G89 now always writes P, and `P0` for a zero dwell.
- The G83 behaviour of #2048 is unchanged (P in ms, `P0` on a zero dwell). No other post file changes. No golden changes, as the body says.
- The pinning tests fail on main's post file. I ran `haas_dwell_cycles` with `origin/main:assets/posts/haas.cps`: 3 failed, 1 passed (`[Some("P500"), None]` against `[Some("P500"), Some("P750")]` and `Some("P0")`). The same-dwell pin passes on both files, which is correct.
- Decision file `docs/decisions/2350-haas-g82-g89-dwell.md` is present. The test file has a provenance line and a Gate map. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` in post code. Body ends `Fixes #2350` and has a `Changelog:` line.

### Results merged with main (locally)
The PR head already contains `origin/main` (trial merge: "Already up to date"). No CR bytes in the three changed files.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all binaries) | 76 binaries, 659 passed, 0 failed |
| `haas_dwell_cycles` (PR head) | 4 passed |
| `haas_dwell_cycles` with main's `haas.cps` | 3 failed, 1 passed (expected) |
| app `conformance` | 7 passed |
| app `haas_machines` | 3 passed |
| app `post_cycle_feed_spindle` | 8 passed |
| app `bore_cycle` | 4 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I also posted local scratch streams (not committed) through the PR's `haas.cps`. Each hole got its own P:
```
G82 ... P500 / G80 / G89 ... P500 / G80 / G82 ... P500 / G80 / G89 ... P0 / G80 / G81 ... (no P) / G80 / G82 ... P250
after T5 M6: G82 ... P500, X Y, X Y / G80 / G89 ... P750 / G80 / G89 ... P0, X Y (same dwell) / G80
G83 ... Q3. P500 / G80 / G83 ... Q3. P0
```
The section end before a tool change writes `G80` and clears the open group (`haas.cps` line 608), so the first hole after a tool change always writes its P.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **`P0` on Haas G89.** The Haas G04 page states "The P values are modal". I did not find Haas text that explicitly accepts `P0` on G82/G89. The Haas mill programming workbook gives dwell values from 0.001 s. Sources: haascnc.com G04 page (`codes-settings.type=gcode.machine=mill.value=G04`) and the Haas mill programming workbook. This is not a blocker: #2048 already posts `P0` on G83, and if a control refuses `P0`, it alarms visibly and does not run a wrong dwell. A possible follow-up: post a zero-dwell back-bore as G85 (feed in, feed out, no dwell word), so the post never needs `P0` on G89.
2. `assets/posts/haas.cps:76`: the comment still says `g|Z|R|Q`. The signature now also has the dwell for G82/G83/G89.
3. **The same stale-P pattern is in other posts.** Each has `sig = g|Z|R|Q` without the dwell, and writes P only when `ms > 0`:
   - `assets/posts/fanuc.cps:1071`
   - `assets/posts/mazak.cps:897`
   - `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps:1233`
   - `assets/posts/grblhal.cps:713`
   - `assets/posts/tormach.cps:1083`

   Two G82/G89 holes with different dwells in one open group post the second hole as a bare `X Y` block. The decision file says the other posts are handled by #2348 and #2349. Those issues cover G83 only, so this G82/G89 defect has no issue. It needs a new issue. Whether P stays modal on each control decides the severity.
4. Haas G85 with a positive dwell still writes P and has no dwell in its signature. The body says this is out of scope (#1445). G85 does not read P on Haas.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
